title: Admin Safeguard Workflow Catalog and Tasklet Orchestrator
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: We have dozens of ad-hoc admin utilities and scripts spread across repos and runbooks. They vary in RBAC checks, lack consistent telemetry, and are brittle when executed in production; this has led to at least two on-call escalations in the last six months.

Proposal: Build an Admin Safeguard Workflow Catalog (ASWC) plus a small Tasklet Orchestrator that surfaces operator-safe tasklets (atomic admin actions) as first-class runbooks-as-tasks. Each tasklet is a manifest (metadata) + implementation bundle and must declare: inputs, outputs, idempotency semantics, required RBAC scope, dry-run mode, telemetry hooks, and a safety policy (pre-checks and approval gates). The catalog is an index and policy-enforcement layer; the orchestrator executes tasklets with sandbox/dry-run support and emits structured telemetry for auditing and regressions.

Goals: centralize admin utilities, reduce mean-time-to-repair for common fixes, eliminate unsafe one-off shell runs, provide audit trail and approval flow, and enable automated remediation for low-risk actions.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog service with REST API and manifest schema v1 deployed to staging
CLI commands: aswc list / aswc run --dry-run / aswc approve implemented
50% of top-40 support playbook steps have a corresponding tasklet or documented exemption
Telemetry: structured events for runlet.start, runlet.finish, runlet.rollback available in prod logging stream
RBAC: policy enforcement test coverage with positive and negative tests
Rollback/abort flow and safety timeouts validated under chaos test
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Spike complete — surveyed 27 admin scripts across infra, ops, and runtime teams. Captured common parameter patterns and failure modes.
2025-02-17: Schema v0.1 draft posted to Confluence: fields for idempotency_token, input_schema (JSON Schema), prechecks, fallback_strategy, required_principal_roles.
2025-02-24: PoC orchestrator implemented as a lightweight HTTP worker + sandbox runner. PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-catalog/pull/212 (WIP).
2025-02-26: Security review kickoff — initial feedback: require signed manifests and optional HSM-based approval for high-risk tasklets.
2025-03-02: Staging integration test: migrated 3 safe-run tasklets (cache-clear, kv-prefix-snapshot, model-rotation-check) and ran dry-run + approval flow successfully.
2025-03-03: Design review with PM and Console team. Feedback: surface runlet metadata in Console runbook editor and show telemetry timeline in route-level dashboard.
decisions: Use a small binary manifest + protobuf for runtime efficiency, with a JSON manifest shim for editing in Console.
Tasklets must declare idempotency semantics; non-idempotent operations require an explicit approval gate before production run.
Prechecks run synchronously before execution; long-running validation (e.g., cross-region capacity) will be async but block final approval.
Telemetry will be structured (JSON) and emitted to the same pipeline as existing runtime traces to simplify correlation.
By default the orchestrator executes in a least-privilege ephemeral container; privileged tasklets require a vetted exception process.
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Gupta) — wants a clear migration plan that prioritizes safety-critical playbooks and low-latency fixes used during incidents.
Security (Rahul Desai) — requires signed manifests and audit trail retention for 1 year; recommend HSM integration for high-risk approvals.
Design (Marta Li) — suggests inline dry-run preview and visible diff between dry-run output and actual run to reduce operator surprises.
SRE (Connor Hayes) — noted performance overhead of synchronous prechecks; recommends batching non-blocking checks or caching precheck results for 5m.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Synchronous prechecks increase latency; tradeoff is safety vs speed during incident remediation.
Signed manifests and HSM approvals add upfront platform complexity but reduce risk of rogue tasklet execution.
Enforcing strict idempotency will require refactoring some legacy scripts; temporary exemption path will be necessary but must be auditable.
Telemetry volume may increase; we will sample low-risk runs and keep full fidelity for high-risk tasklets.
next_steps: Finalize manifest schema v1 and publish JSON <-> protobuf conversion tooling (owner: eng-platform).
Complete PR build-out for PoC and move to canary in staging (owner: Ethan Caldwell).
Implement signed-manifest flow and HSM approval integration for high-risk tags (owner: security infra).
Create migration plan for top-40 playbook steps, schedule pair-programming with support engineers for knowledge transfer.
Add Console surface: runlet inspector and approval UI + console telemetry timeline (owner: console team).
Define retention and audit log policy and get sign-off from legal/compliance.
